subject: Medieval History
sub_topic: Krishna Deva Raya — administration and literature

concepts.name: Krishna Deva Raya's Political Titles and Legitimacy
key_dimensions: Title 'Kannada Rajya Rama Ramana' and its cultural-political significance
Use of 'Abhinava Bhoja' and 'Andhra Bhoja' — multilingual patronage claims
How titles were used to legitimize rule over diverse linguistic groups
UPSC Trap: Distinguishing his titles from those of other Vijayanagara rulers like Deva Raya II

concepts.name: Ashtadiggajas — The Eight Poets of Krishna Deva Raya's Court
key_dimensions: Names and works of all eight poets (e.g., Allasani Peddana, Nandi Timmana, Tenali Ramakrishna)
Peddana as 'Andhra Kavita Pitamaha' and his work Manucharitra (Svaroochi Sambhava)
Distinction between their individual literary contributions and genres
UPSC Trap: Confusing which poet wrote which work — e.g., Nandi Timmana's Parijatapaharanam vs. others

concepts.name: Amuktamalyada — Krishna Deva Raya's Own Literary Work
key_dimensions: Language (Telugu), genre (Prabandha kavya), and theme (devotion to Vishnu/Andal)
Political philosophy embedded in the text — advice on statecraft and diplomacy
Significance as a ruler personally contributing to Telugu literature
UPSC Trap: Distinguishing Amuktamalyada from his Sanskrit work Jambavati Kalyanam

concepts.name: Jambavati Kalyanam — Krishna Deva Raya's Sanskrit Contribution
key_dimensions: Genre: Sanskrit drama depicting Krishna's marriage to Jambavati
Demonstrates the ruler's bilingual (Telugu + Sanskrit) literary capability
Its role in establishing royal prestige through classical Sanskrit tradition
UPSC Trap: Often overlooked in favor of Amuktamalyada; both are his works but in different languages

concepts.name: Administrative Divisions under Krishna Deva Raya
key_dimensions: Hierarchical structure: Rajya/Mandala → Nadu → Sthala → Grама
Role of Nayakas (provincial governors) and their semi-autonomous nature
Revenue administration and land measurement practices
UPSC Trap: Confusing the Vijayanagara Nayaka system with the later independent Nayaka kingdoms

concepts.name: Nayankara System — Military-Administrative Framework
key_dimensions: Definition: Land grants (amaram) given to Nayakas in exchange for military service
Comparison with the feudal system and the Delhi Sultanate's iqta system
How it created both administrative efficiency and seeds of political fragmentation
UPSC Trap: Distinguishing Nayankara (military assignment) from Umbali (service tenure grants)

concepts.name: Revenue System and Taxation under Krishna Deva Raya
key_dimensions: Land tax as primary revenue; categories of taxable land
Trade taxes, tolls, and their role in a commercially active economy
Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz accounts on the prosperity of the empire
UPSC Trap: Attributing specific revenue reforms to Krishna Deva Raya vs. earlier/later rulers

concepts.name: Military Organization and Conquests
key_dimensions: Conquest of Raichur Doab (1512) — strategic significance against Bijapur Sultanate
Orissa campaign and defeat of Gajapati king Prataparudra; treaty and marriage alliance
Composition of army: infantry, cavalry, war elephants, and use of Portuguese firearms
UPSC Trap: The Raichur Battle (1520) — often confused with earlier or later Deccan conflicts

concepts.name: Diplomatic Relations with Portuguese
key_dimensions: Alliance of convenience: Krishna Deva Raya allowed Portuguese horse trade to counter Deccan Sultans
Strategic import of Arabian horses through Goa (Portuguese-controlled)
Limits of the alliance — no formal treaty, purely transactional
UPSC Trap: Over-stating the alliance as a formal political partnership vs. a commercial arrangement

concepts.name: Policy Toward the Deccan Sultanates
key_dimensions: Exploiting divisions among the five Deccan Sultanates (post-Bahmani fragmentation)
'Mitra Dharma' policy — supporting weaker sultans against stronger ones
Defeat of Bidar, Bijapur, and Golconda at various points
UPSC Trap: The policy of balance of power vs. outright conquest — Krishna Deva Raya rarely sought annexation of sultanate territories

concepts.name: Telugu Literature's 'Golden Age' — Contextualizing Krishna Deva Raya's Reign
key_dimensions: Why his reign is called the 'Golden Age of Telugu Literature'
Shift from champu style to Prabandha (ornate) style of Telugu poetry
Role of royal patronage in standardizing literary forms
UPSC Trap: Conflating the 'Golden Age of Telugu' with the entire Vijayanagara period rather than specifically his reign

concepts.name: Tenali Ramakrishna — Court Jester, Poet, and Satirist
key_dimensions: His work Panduranga Mahatmyamu and Vaishnava devotional context
Dual identity: one of the Ashtadiggajas yet also known for wit and satire
Historical person vs. legendary figure — separating fact from folklore for UPSC
UPSC Trap: His works are often misattributed or his role as a serious poet is underestimated

concepts.name: Allasani Peddana and Manucharitra
key_dimensions: Full title: Svaroochi Sambhava Manucharitra — its theme and poetic style
Why Peddana is called 'Andhra Kavita Pitamaha' (grandfather of Telugu poetry)
Prabandha style characteristics as seen in Manucharitra
UPSC Trap: Confusing Peddana's incomplete work (completed by Krishna Deva Raya himself, per tradition) with fully authored texts

concepts.name: Architecture and Temple Construction under Krishna Deva Raya
key_dimensions: Construction of Vittala Temple complex and Hazara Rama Temple at Hampi
Unique Vijayanagara style: fusion of Chalukya, Hoysala, and Dravidian elements
Gopuram-centric temple architecture vs. earlier styles
UPSC Trap: Attributing specific temples to Krishna Deva Raya vs. other Vijayanagara rulers — Vittala Temple predates him but he expanded it

concepts.name: Foreign Traveller Accounts — Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz
key_dimensions: Paes: Description of Vijayanagara city's grandeur, markets, and the Mahanavami festival
Nuniz: Administrative structure, military, and succession disputes
How these accounts corroborate or contradict indigenous sources
UPSC Trap: Paes visited during Krishna Deva Raya's reign; Nuniz visited slightly later — their temporal contexts matter

concepts.name: Role of Women and Mahila Bureaucracy
key_dimensions: Accounts of women serving as royal bodyguards, accountants, and wrestlers (per Paes)
Status of women in administration — unique feature noted by foreign visitors
Comparison with women's roles in other medieval Indian kingdoms
UPSC Trap: This is often presented as exaggerated; UPSC may test whether candidates can critically evaluate such accounts

concepts.name: Krishna Deva Raya's Statecraft Philosophy — Amuktamalyada as Political Text
key_dimensions: Advice on choosing ministers, conducting diplomacy, and treating subordinates
The concept of 'Kutila Niti' (shrewd diplomacy) vs. open warfare
Comparison with Kautilya's Arthashastra and its influence on his governance
UPSC Trap: Treating Amuktamalyada purely as a devotional text while missing its embedded political philosophy

concepts.name: Succession Crisis and Post-Krishna Deva Raya Decline
key_dimensions: Conflict between Aliya Rama Raya and other claimants after Krishna Deva Raya's death (1529)
How personal rule dependence created institutional weakness
Link between post-1529 instability and the eventual Battle of Talikota (1565)
UPSC Trap: Attributing the fall of Vijayanagara to the Battle of Talikota alone, ignoring the internal decay that began after 1529

concepts.name: Krishna Deva Raya's Religious Policy — Vaishnava Patronage and Tolerance
key_dimensions: Personal devotion to Lord Venkateshwara (Tirupati) and Vaishnavism
Yet patronized Shaivite temples and Muslim soldiers in his army
Use of religion as a tool of political legitimacy vs. genuine personal faith
UPSC Trap: Labeling him as exclusively Vaishnava ignores his broad-based religious patronage
